title: a foreign decorator is a foreign call: it is invoked when the declaration it decorates is evaluated
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." poc/src/language/README.md names the decorator as the third spelling that reaches `SMITHERS1504` with no call expression at all. The diagnostic is charged at the decorator and no `SMITHERS1101` accompanies it because the invocation happens as the module is evaluated rather than inside any function's row — which is also why it is worse than an ordinary unchecked call: there is no enclosing contract that could have carried the channel. These are ECMAScript decorators, not the legacy TypeScript ones: specification/compatibility.mdx §Configuration lists `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` among the FORBIDDEN options.
